chapter: Third reel: musicians and George Girard
title: Mellophone players and Monk Hable
summary: Talk of hot mellophone players, including drummer Monk Hable who played a jazz chorus on one.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You know, when I asked you about the mellophone I wanted to mention to you was it uh, uh, how do you call it? Uh, Dudley Fosdick used to play mellophone with Lombardo. And there are very few hot mellophone players that I ever knew in my life. And I just wondered how many you knew who played mellophone around town.

I don't recall seeing it but you said he played it with a lombardo band. Now he may have had it on the side. He might have played trumpet and mellophone, which I've seen happen. Yeah. In fact the late Monk Hable was the drummer at the famous store for many years. And Monk had an old mellophone on the side which he picked up and played a beautiful jazz chorus on. Oh yeah. If you ever heard of that, I don't know if you know about that.

Oh sure, well I knew Monk. He was the first jazz musician in New Orleans that I ever got to know was Monk. And that was when he was working on Broadway in the Alcohol Factory. Right. Walking around in it all day long.
